thread:
oliver: Heads-up 1 I opened a docs PR to clean up Dedicated provisioning: adjust autoscale cooldown defaults, add a tiny isolation manifest example, swap in the new unified SDK snippet, and repair a couple broken handbook links. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4198
raya: Thanks 1 I'll take the first pass today. Can you enumerate the exact checklist items so I can mark them in the PR description? :clipboard:
oliver: Sure 1 Checklist bullets: 1) explain cooldown vs burst windows (defaults and examples), 2) include a minimal tenant labels example (isolation + eviction hint), 3) replace deprecated JS SDK call with unified SDK pattern, 4) fix two handbook anchors flagged by link-checker, 5) update SLA wording per legal.
sasha: The link-checker flagged an old anchor for the reserved pools eviction section. I already updated the runbook anchor last week2E Use https://handbook.redwood.ai/reserved-pools#eviction-behavior instead of the old path.
docs-bot: Link-check results: 2 broken links found in docs/dedicated/provisioning.md: line 170 -> /handbook/reserved-pools#eviction (404), line 231 -> /sdk/js#deprecatedCreateScalePolicy (404). Auto-suggested replacements attached.
mike: Legal/제품 note: don't promise hard latency guarantees in the SLA text. Use the agreed phrasing from the product SLA doc. I'll paste the approved sentence.
oliver: Pasting the new unified JS SDK snippet to include in the PR (keep minimal):

```js
// create autoscale policy (unified SDK)
import Redwood from '@redwoodhq/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
await client.dedicated.createScalePolicy({
  tenantId: 'tenant-123',
  policy: {
    minGPUs: 1,
    maxGPUs: 8,
    cooldownSeconds: 300,
    burstWindowSeconds: 60
  }
})
```

raya: Nice and compact. I'll paste that and switch to const names that match our examples. For the isolation snippet, propose a short YAML manifest showing labels and a comment for eviction preference:

```yaml
# tenant manifest (snippet)
tenant_id: tenant-123
labels:
  isolation: dedicated
  env: prod
# eviction_preference: prefer-non-isolated
```

sasha: Small editorial note: call out that labels are indexed and used by scale-policy routing and placement. One sentence in the doc should cover that.
mike: Approved SLA phrasing (from product doc): "We aim for 99.9% uptime on Dedicated capacity. Latency is covered by model-class SLOs in the SLA matrix; we do not guarantee hard latency bounds." Please include exactly and link to the SLA matrix.
oliver: Good2E I'll add that sentence and link. Also decided to add two short bullets under "what happens when tenants exceed quota" so users know fallback behavior. Raya, can you add these bullets?
raya: Sure. Suggested bullets:
- Automatic fallback to a compatible, smaller model variant when configured (cost-optimized path).
- Requests queued with a Retry-After header when no compatible variant is available.

raya: Also I'll run the repo link-checker locally after making the edits before requesting reviews.
sasha: One more nit: in the autoscale section, mention the interaction between cooldown and burstWindow: burst allows short token spikes but cooldown prevents immediate subsequent scale-ups. A single example line will help.
oliver: I'll draft that example sentence: "Example: with cooldownSeconds=300 and burstWindowSeconds=60, the fleet may briefly expand to handle 60s spikes, but will not trigger another scale-up for 300s after a confirmed scale event." Feel free to reword.
mike: Once PR is updated, assign reviewers: @sasha for handbook anchors/links, @mike for SLA phrasing, @docs for final copy check.
oliver: Plan: raya updates snippets + anchor fixes + SLA sentence by EOD, pushes commit to PR, requests reviews. Ping if blocked. :thumbsup:
